subject: Cross-border evidence custody & notification ladder — FinBound
messages:
From: Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@finbound.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@finbound.com>
Date: Wed, 14 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on notification ladder & evidence custody for DPA

Sean —

Thanks for taking this while we work through the DPA redlines. Attached is a short pack of questions from our legal/security teams (FinBound_DPA_questions.pdf). High level asks:

- Notification windows: our DPA expects a 48–72 hour substantive notification for incidents impacting customer data. We need clarity on Redwood's operational definition of ‘notification’ vs ‘initial triage flag’.
- Evidence custody: if an incident involves EU data, FinBound must be able to request a forensics snapshot preserved in-region (EU) until transfer approvals are completed. Can Redwood support an EU-escrow or controlled handover?
- Subprocessor cooperation: how quickly can subprocessors provide preserved telemetry and logs when requested under the DPA?

Practical question: is there a named Redwood contact for incident coordination + a runbook for evidence transfer? If you can outline the ladder of notifications (triage / customer-facing / regulatory) we can align on the SLA language.

Appreciate a quick confirmation of next steps — Marcus and I will need this to finalize the amendment.

Alicia Ramos
CISO, FinBound
[Attachment: FinBound_DPA_questions.pdf]
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
To: Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@finbound.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 14 May 2025 11:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on notification ladder & evidence custody for DPA

Alicia — thanks for the doc and the clear asks. Looping Ben (Head of Security Ops) and Kimberly (Privacy & Compliance) so we can align on both operational runbook and contract language.

Quick summary of what we can commit to today and open items:

1) Notification ladder
- Initial triage flag: we can send an automated triage notice within 24 hours that a potential incident has been detected and is being investigated (this contains scope estimate and affected model/tenant hash).
- Substantive customer notification: we typically target 72 hours from detection for a customer-facing notification when we can reasonably confirm impact and scope. For confirmed exfiltration of customer data we will escalate and shorten that window where feasible.

2) Evidence custody and in-region preservation
- We can preserve forensic snapshots and KV-cache extracts for 30 days by default and extend on request.
- For EU-data-specific preservation: we can retain evidence in an EU region and provide controlled access/export under lawful basis / customer-approved export authorization. We need to formalize the mechanism (secure SFTP to customer escrow, or a staged download via our EU evidence node).

3) Subprocessor cooperation
- We require subprocessors to respond to evidence preservation requests within 48 hours for acknowledgement and within 7 business days for handover of most logs. Some third parties (cloud infra) may have constraints that extend timelines; we'll flag those in the subprocessor roster.

Open asks from our side:
- Can FinBound accept a 72-hour substantive notification SLO in the DPA with a 24-hour triage/flag requirement?
- For evidence handover, please confirm whether you prefer (a) SFTP to your EU escrow node, (b) staged encrypted transfer to a Redwood-approved third‑party escrow, or (c) access to an EU-hosted download bundle behind an authenticated portal.

Next steps: Ben and Kimberly will draft the runbook and a short redline for the DPA section that captures the triage vs substantive notification language and the evidence handover options. If you can indicate preference on the transfer mechanism today we can include it in our proposal.

Sean Gallagher
Director, Account Security — Redwood Inference

Sean/Ben/Kimberly —

Thanks for the quick response. A few clarifications from FinBound legal/security:

- 72 hours for substantive notification is acceptable as long as the DPA calls out the 24-hour triage flag and an obligation to update the customer at pre-defined milestones (24h, 72h, 7d).
- Evidence custody: FinBound's preference is (a) SFTP to our EU escrow node — we will provide credentials and an ingestion path. We also require a written chain-of-custody record and a custody hash for any snapshot.
- Subprocessor timelines: 7 business days is pushing it for certain regulated partners; can Redwood commit to expedited escalation (internal SLA) to prioritize FinBound requests? We understand some third parties will still impose delays; we need a documented escalation ladder.

Attached a short form we use for evidence requests (evidence-request-form.docx) so your ops team can see the metadata we need. Also: can you provide the current subprocessor roster (redwood_subprocessors_public.csv or link) and the SOC 2 auditor contact for corroboration?

If you can send a runbook draft by EOD Friday (local), we can circulate internally and aim to sign the amendment next week.

Alicia Ramos
CISO, FinBound
[Attachment: evidence-request-form.docx]

Alicia / Marcus —

Appreciate the signal and the form — that was helpful. Action items and commitments from Redwood:

- Contract language: we will propose DPA language that codifies a 24-hour triage flag + 72-hour substantive notification with milestone updates at 24h/72h/7d. Where evidence indicates higher urgency we will accelerate.

- Evidence preservation & handover: Redwood can accept secure SFTP ingestion to your EU escrow node. We will provide a custody manifest (SHA256 hashes for bundles) and a chain-of-custody record for any snapshot we provide. We will also offer an alternative option: temporary access to an encrypted EU-hosted download bundle if SFTP proves infeasible.

- Subprocessors: attached is our evidence-handling checklist and the current public subprocessor roster link (redacted for this thread). We will commit to an internal 48-hour escalation acknowledgement to prioritize FinBound requests; final handover timeframes for specific third parties will be captured per-subprocessor in the runbook.

Attachments: redwood-evidence-handling-checklist.pdf

Next steps: Kimberly will attach a redline for the DPA section and Ben will coordinate a short runbook (private link) that maps roles (Redwood incident commander, security ops point, privacy liaison) to contact info and tooling for transfer. Can you confirm the SFTP host & preferred credentials format (key vs password)? Once we have that we'll run a dry‑run handover with your infra team before signing.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Head of Security Ops — Redwood Inference
